My Workspace

Demo Manager · Demo User · Proposed GMS architecture & personal local AI stack

Proposal - pending GMS IT / Security / Legal review. Not yet implemented. The Claude API option requires a corporate DPA with Anthropic (Swiss nDSG compliance), no-training guarantees and an EU data region.
Two deployment options

Option A - Local AI Stack

Self-hosted on GMS servers. Maximum data sovereignty.
100% data sovereignty - nothing leaves GMS; nDSG compliant without a DPA
Zero per-query cost - runs on GMS hardware; works offline
Full control - GMS owns the model; can fine-tune / customize
AI quality: good (Llama / Mistral / Qwen) - needs tuning
Maintenance high; scalability limited by hardware
Setup 4-6 weeks ~Zero per-query

Option B - Anthropic Claude API RECOMMENDED

Cloud API under corporate contract. Best quality, fastest path.
Production quality day 1 - Claude Sonnet 4.6; best reasoning & multi-document analysis
Corporate Anthropic Enterprise contract - DPA + NDA + SLA; nDSG (Swiss law); GMS AG signs directly
API key server-side only - Azure AD access control; full audit log
Zero model maintenance - Anthropic maintains models; auto-scales
Requires internet; usage-based billing
2-3 weeks ~$365-2,000/mo
Recommended path: sign the Anthropic Enterprise agreement (DPA + NDA + SLA) now → deploy Option B in Q3 2026 → re-evaluate Option A migration in 2027 based on volume and data-sovereignty needs.

The platform is designed to be implemented fully in line with Demo knowledge source policies and procedures and to meet all applicable security and data-protection standards. Access is role-based (Azure AD), every request is audited, and the Claude API option is covered by a corporate Anthropic agreement (DPA + NDA + SLA) with EU / Swiss data residency - subject to Information Security and Legal sign-off.

Closed local contour - sensitive / GMS data and code stay on local compute (owned or rented), never in the cloud. Models run fully offline (Ollama / LM Studio + AnythingLLM). The Claude API is not used for GMS data.
This demo was built on this stack. The Helix dashboard you are viewing - its data structure, architecture and content - was designed and produced locally with the tools below.
Call flow
Obsidian
Structured knowledge
AnythingLLM
RAG + embeddings
Ollama / LM Studio
Local LLM - offline
Outputs
Analysis - Excel - reports
A query reads the structured knowledge indexed in Obsidian, AnythingLLM retrieves the relevant chunks via local embeddings, the local LLM (Ollama / LM Studio) generates the answer fully offline, and the result is delivered as analysis or an Excel / PDF report.
Software stack

Inference engines

Ollama - runs the local model; OpenAI-compatible API (:11434) - integration hub for every tool
LM Studio - GUI runtime + model browser; same models, easier control
llama.cpp / GGUF - the underlying engine; runs Q4_K_M quantized models efficiently

Models (local, offline)

Qwen3 14B - general reasoning: traffic / margin analysis, summaries
Qwen2.5-Coder 14B - generates dashboards, parsers, automations
Qwen2.5-VL 7B - vision: reads Excel / PPT / screenshots into data
nomic-embed-text / bge-m3 - embeddings that power RAG search
bge-reranker - reorders retrieved chunks for answer precision

RAG & knowledge

Obsidian - local knowledge base. Built from own domain expertise and a purpose-designed data structure / architecture, organized into documents that feed the model context
AnythingLLM - indexes the vault and answers questions over it (LanceDB vector store)
Qdrant - scalable vector DB (Docker) when the corpus outgrows LanceDB
OpenWebUI - chat front-end for the local Ollama models

Build & automation

Continue.dev - AI coding inside the editor, backed by local Ollama - keeps GMS code on-machine
n8n - local automation: daily summaries, ticket creation, scheduled reports
Docker - runs and orchestrates the local services (n8n, Qdrant, OpenWebUI)
For GMS TZ / specs this local contour is the approved architecture: Obsidian + GMS files + sensitive data → AnythingLLM (RAG, local embeddings) + Ollama / LM Studio (offline) → outputs (traffic analysis, pricing / reports, RAG search over contracts). Any cloud tool and the Claude API stay outside the GMS contour.
Compliance & governance
Because everything runs inside GMS infrastructure and no data leaves the company, the local stack aligns with Demo knowledge source policies and procedures by design and meets data-protection standards without a third-party processor - no external DPA required. Access control and audit are enforced at the application layer.
